why: A grid DP where the state is a shape, not a path: side[r][c] = the largest all-ones square whose bottom-right corner is (r, c), which is 1 + the minimum of the three neighbours above, left and diagonal. It also equals the number of squares ending at that corner.
hints: Fix the bottom-right corner of a square. How many all-ones squares end there?
If (r, c) is 1, side[r][c] = 1 + min(side[r-1][c], side[r][c-1], side[r-1][c-1]); the squares ending there have sides 1..side[r][c].
Sum side[r][c] over all cells, keeping one previous row. O(rows * cols).
pitfalls: The answer is a count of squares, not the largest area.
Cells that are 0 have side 0 and break every square through them.
